reviewNote: THE TERMINAL PAGE OF THE WALK. Captured live 2026-07-15 on throwaway draft 13218429 (client Individual 'test, test'), which was EMPTY apart from the auto-created draft — hence the 14 red alerts and the disabled Next. Reached by CLICKING the sidebar 'Review your application' link on a brand-new draft: it does NOT bounce to the form start, so unlike the I-130's conditional/evidence pages this page has no anti-deep-linking prerequisite (a direct URL load also holds). Renders NO inputs (fields: []) — nothing to type, nothing to map to a fact_key.
advanceControlNote: SAFETY-CRITICAL. The control that advances PAST review is a plain 'Next' — id=button-button, data-testid=next-button — i.e. BYTE-IDENTICAL to the Next on every other page of the form. It carries no 'Submit'/'Pay'/'Sign' text, so fill-chain's NEVER_CLICK_TEXT guard CANNOT catch it, and findNextButton() matches it on its FIRST selector (button[data-testid='next-button']). It is disabled here only because the empty draft has red alerts; USCIS enables it once the application has no alerts — precisely the state a successful autofill run produces. The descriptor entry (kind: 'review') is therefore the ONLY thing that stops the walk here; the text guard is a backstop for the pages DOWNSTREAM of this one, not for this one.

downstreamRoutes.note: NOT VISITED — read out of the myUSCIS client route table (packs/js/index-*.js), which is shared across all myUSCIS forms, so not every route below is an I-539 route. Recorded to document what clicking Next here would lead into. The sidebar lists ONE page under 'Review and Submit' ('Review your application'), so review itself is a SINGLE screen; the sign/pay steps are separate routes not shown in the sidebar.
